items.title: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
items.summary: The talks come as Ukraine reels from a deadly Russian strike on a village in Zaporizhzhia last week, in which at least 40 people were killed Trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have begun in Abu Dhabi Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said yesterday that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine "An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X Ahead of the meeting, the two US envoys met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials in Abu Dhabi, and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was adamant that France, the UK and Germany "will indeed be in the…

items.title: COP31: Mozambique seeks increased climate finance for vulnerable countries
items.summary: In a statement, the Presidency said that Daniel Chapo would take part in several high-level meetings and events held as part of the COP31 conference, dedicated to discussing global challenges and responses to climate change “Mozambique’s participation in this summit aims to reaffirm the country’s national commitment to global climate action and mobilise international cooperation to address the impacts of climate change, with particular attention to the need to strengthen climate finance for the most vulnerable countries,” the statement reads READ: Mozambique: President Chapo heads to Antalya for COP31 climate summit The World Climate Action Summit, which forms part of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), is taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, until 20 November.

items.title: DR Congo: 66 soldiers sentenced to death for cowardice in conflict with FRN rebels
items.summary: Dozens of defendants were put on trial over accusations that they abandoned their posts and refused to follow direct orders Some 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death in DR Congo on charged of cowardice, mutiny, and failure to obey orders. The sentence was handed down by the Goma Garrison Military Court At least 71 members of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) were arrested in several separate incidents related to the fierce fighting between the military and rebel groups near the country's borders with Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi They were arrested on allegations of abandoning their posts or running away from clashes with FRN rebels. Prosecutors had sought capital punishment for 70 of the defendants, while asking for a 10-year jail term for an intelligence officer.

items.title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
items.summary: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't A gunman killed six people in a shooting spree in Krakow's Old Town on Saturday, before being shot and detained by police. The gunman, who is also suspected of killing three family members before the attack, later died in hospital On Monday, Poland's national prosecutor's office announced a formal investigation Nevertheless, much is still unknown about the details of the crime, leaving social media users to fill the information vacuum with fake images of the attacker and alleged screenshots of his online profile. DW Fact Check breaks down the developing story Claim: A viral picture has been circulating on social media claiming to be the real image of the suspected attacker But the unusual sharpness of this picture raises doubt of its authenticity. It is difficult to imagine capturing such a clear image in a chaotic situation DW checked the image using two different AI detectors.

items.title: Watch: Man smashes Chinese government building with excavator
items.summary: Police in China's Shaanxi province say they have detained a 47-year-old man for damaging a government building with "construction machinery" on Monday afternoon Videos circulating on social media show an excavator tearing down the facade of the building. Local media reported that staff inside the building were urgently evacuated No one was injured in the incident, said the police, who did not provide a motive for the act

items.title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election
items.summary: Voters cast their ballots at a polling station during South Africa's local government elections in Johannesburg South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic" While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 31% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 65% 20 years ago The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second in the overall vote with 25%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town.
